subject: Oceanography
title: Submarine Volcanoes
description: A quick win: understand Submarine Volcanoes.

hook.text: More than 80% of volcanic eruptions on Earth happen underwater—unseen and unheard.

buildup.text: Most submarine volcanoes erupt along mid-ocean ridges, where tectonic plates pull apart.

discovery.text: Pillow lavas form when hot magma meets cold seawater—solidifying into rounded, pillow-shaped mounds.

twist.text: In 1963, a submarine eruption built the island of Surtsey off Iceland—an island born in four years.

climax.text: Submarine eruptions add new crust, release heat, inject minerals, and create habitats.

punchline.text: Most of Earth's volcanism happens where no one can see it.

quiz.question: What are pillow lavas?
options: Rounded lava shapes formed by rapid cooling in seawater
